title: Why the $149 Tier Exists Only to Sell You the $79 Plan
alt_title_1: Dan Ariely's MIT Decoy Pricing Trick Exposed
alt_title_2: How Price Anchoring Hijacks Your Brain at Checkout
description_hook: That overpriced $149 top tier on software and subscription pages is rarely meant to be bought - it is an anchor planted to make $79 feel cheap. Here is MIT economist Dan Ariely's Decoy Effect study and the Blank-Sheet Rule.

scenes.headline: The Overpriced Tier Nobody Is Meant to Buy
scenes.stat_label: PLANTED TO MAKE $79 FEEL LIKE A STEAL
bullets: Top pricing tiers often exist purely as psychological contrast
You measure the middle option against the anchor, not reality
scenes.narration: Have you ever noticed a pricing page with an overpriced hundred-forty-nine-dollar tier that almost nobody needs? You are not meant to buy it - you are meant to measure against it.

scenes.headline: Dan Ariely's MIT Economist Experiment
scenes.stat_label: CHOSE PREMIUM WHEN DECOY WAS PRESENT
bullets: With a decoy tier visible, 84% picked the expensive bundle
Remove the decoy tier, and only 32% paid the premium price
scenes.narration: MIT economist Dan Ariely proved why in Predictably Irrational. When he placed a useless decoy option beside a premium magazine bundle, eighty-four percent of readers chose the expensive plan. Without the decoy, only thirty-two percent did.

scenes.headline: Relative Bargains vs Absolute Utility
scenes.right_body: Ignore crossed-out prices -> judge real monthly utility
scenes.narration: Psychologists call this Price Anchoring. Your brain struggles to calculate standalone value, so sellers plant a high anchor first to make seventy-nine dollars feel cheap.

scenes.headline: Run the Blank-Sheet Ceiling Test
scenes.stat_subtext: Price the problem blind -> pocket the spread every month
scenes.narration: Use the Blank-Sheet Test before any purchase: cover the pricing table, write down what solving that exact problem is worth to you, and reject anything above it.

scenes.headline: Fake Discounts Still Drain Real Margin
scenes.stat_label: NEVER BUY RELATIVE TO AN ANCHOR
bullets: Crossed-out MSRPs and extreme tiers are comparison traps
Set your walk-away price before looking at the menu
scenes.narration: A steep discount off a fake anchor is still a real leak. Keep that in mind, because...
